display_name: Munim Khan vs Daud Khan Karrani
one_line: Two rival commanders facing off in the Mughal conquest of Bengal, 1575–1576 CE: Munim Khan, Akbar’s veteran general, and Daud Khan Karrani, the last Afghan sultan of Bengal.

appearance.age_look: Munim Khan appears in his late 50s with a sturdy, slightly heavy build; Daud Khan appears in his early 30s with a lean, athletic build.
appearance.face: Munim Khan has an oval face, medium-tan North Indian complexion, thick grey moustache with a neatly trimmed short grey beard, faint crow’s-feet at the eyes, and a calm, assessing default expression; Daud Khan has a sharper, heart-shaped face, slightly deeper wheatish complexion, a prominent nose, black arched brows, a well-groomed black moustache with a short pointed beard, and a proud, intense default expression.
appearance.hair: Munim Khan’s hair is mostly hidden under a tall, slightly conical red velvet Mughal turban with a cream cloth band and a small emerald-and-gold turban jewel at the front; a hint of short greying hair shows at the nape; Daud Khan’s long black hair is tied back in a low knot under a dark green Afghan-style turban wrapped flatter and wider, with the end tail draped over his left shoulder and a small silver crescent brooch on the side.
appearance.costume: Munim Khan wears a long, knee-length Mughal jama of rich deep maroon silk with fine diagonal gold-thread stripes, fastening to his right, over a light cream cotton inner tunic and straight cream churidar trousers; a broad dark green silk patka (waist sash) with subtle gold floral motifs wraps his waist, knotted slightly to the left with its ends hanging; over the jama he has a sleeveless quilted light-olive-coloured cotton coat that suggests padded armour without metal plates; he wears soft brown leather ankle boots and a simple dark leather belt supporting a scabbard; Daud Khan wears a calf-length dark teal cotton tunic with side slits, cut looser than the Mughal jama, over off-white tight trousers, a wide dark brown leather belt with a simple rectangular brass buckle, and a sleeveless brown leather lamellar-style over-vest with small overlapping rectangular leather scales stitched in rows to evoke Afghan armour; his forearms carry bracer-like dark leather wraps, and he wears dark brown leather boots that reach mid-calf.
appearance.signature: Munim Khan’s signature prop is a slightly curved Mughal talwar with a simple steel blade and a gold-hilted Indo-Muslim basket hilt, carried in a plain brown leather scabbard at his left hip, while Daud Khan’s signature weapon is a long straight Afghan-style spear with a leaf-shaped steel head and a dark wooden shaft bound with narrow leather bands near the grip.

ref_desc: Munim Khan is a late-middle-aged, medium-tan Mughal general with a red turban, maroon striped jama, olive quilted sleeveless coat, cream churidar, brown boots, and a gold-hilted talwar, facing Daud Khan, a younger, wheatish Afghan in a dark green turban, teal tunic, brown lamellar leather vest, off-white trousers, brown boots, and wielding a long straight spear; both share a palette of maroon, dark teal, cream, olive, and dark green.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet featuring two historically grounded late-16th-century north Indian commanders standing side by side, shown from head to toe in a neutral pose with clear details. The older man, Munim Khan, has an oval face, medium-tan complexion, thick grey moustache and short grey beard, with calm, focused eyes; his hair is mostly hidden under a tall, slightly conical red velvet Mughal turban wrapped with a cream band and set with a small emerald-and-gold jewel at the front. He wears a deep maroon silk knee-length jama with fine diagonal gold stripes, fastening on the right, over a light cream inner tunic and cream churidar trousers; a wide dark green silk patka with subtle gold floral motifs wraps his waist, knotted to the left so its ends hang; over this is a sleeveless light-olive quilted cotton coat suggesting padded armour, and he has soft brown leather ankle boots and a dark leather belt holding a plain brown leather scabbard with a slightly curved steel talwar, its hilt gold-toned with a basket-like Indo-Muslim guard. Beside him, Daud Khan is lean and intense, with a heart-shaped face, slightly deeper wheatish complexion, sharp nose, black arched brows, and a black moustache with a short pointed beard; his long black hair is tied back in a low knot under a wide, flatter dark green Afghan-style turban whose tail drapes over his left shoulder and bears a small silver crescent brooch. He wears a dark teal calf-length cotton tunic with side slits over off-white tight trousers, a wide dark brown leather belt with a brass buckle, and a sleeveless brown leather lamellar vest made of overlapping rectangular leather scales; his forearms are wrapped in dark leather bracers and his mid-calf brown leather boots are plain but sturdy. His signature weapon is a long straight wooden-shafted spear with a leaf-shaped steel head and leather binding around the grip, held upright in his right hand. Use a harmonious palette of deep maroon, dark teal, cream, olive, and dark green, and keep the overall design dignified, historically plausible for the Mughal–Afghan frontier circa 1575–1576, and easily redrawn consistently across panels.
